newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called to open flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called to open flat to higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat to higher Tuesday following yesterday's light, rangebound session that ended slightly lower amid softer cash prices and natural gas futures.
"People are coming in to cover (their May positions)," said a West Coast paper broker.

In over-the-counter business, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $13.50-14.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Monday's settlement at $13.30, while June Palo Verde (PV) at $18.40-18.55 against yesterday's close at $18.28.
May COB prices, in the paper market, were assessed at $14.60-14.80 and May PV at $18.20-18.50.
Market sources said June futures would likely take cue in the short-term from the cash and natgas prices.
The June Henry Hub gas contract opened down 1.1 cent at $2.070 per million British thermal units.

In the Northwest, temperatures would stay four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal through Wednesday and moderate to normal to four degrees below normal Thursday into the weekend. Unstable atmospheric conditions could bring chance of rain along the coast and in the mountains.
In the Southwest, dry and mild weather would settle over the southern part of the region for the rest of the week with readings averaging three to five degrees F above normal.
Cloudy skies and slightly cooler-than-normal weather were predicted for Utah, Colorado and northern California.
